recipes.name: Balsamic Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant but not brown, about 2 minutes.

Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to release their juices, about 2 minutes. Stir in balsamic vinegar and wine; cook until mushrooms are tender, about 2 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Balsamic mushrooms sautéed in a garlicky sauce make the perfect appetizer. Serve them either hot or cold before your next dinner party or special occasion.

review.reviewBody: i sauteed diced onions until they carmelized then added the garlic, then the balsamic and wine, then the mushrooms to add a carmelized flavor. also, i used less oil to make the dish lowfat. it tasted great!

I followed the recipe as written, however, I needed to adjust proportionately since I had 1.25 pounds of sliced mushrooms. I used a Chardonnay wine and 18-year aged balsamic vinegar. This recipe is very easy to make and it tastes great. I selected this particular recipe because it says it is good warm or cold. I plan to use it cold on an antipasto in two days. I am assuming it will only improve in flavor due to the extra marinating & chilling time!

I took into consideration some of the mixed reviews when preparing this recipe. I had a pound of fresh baby bella mushrooms, sliced. 1/3 cup of olive oil is a lot of oil so I eyeballed mine, 2 T in a skillet. Once heated I added the sliced mushrooms, then a couple of sliced garlic, stirring everything. I grinded some fresh ground black pepper on top of the mushrooms. Did not add any salt. I added 2T of white wine and 1T of baslsamic vinegar. I also added a tiny pinch of white sugar to shave off that edge of "tang" from the vinegar. I am so glad that I did not add the full 3T of Balsamic called for in this recipe. The combination of seasonings blended well- a nice rich depth of flavors. These mushrooms were delicious and complemented my steaks, "Roasted Tomatoes with Garlic", and "Ciabatta Bread", also from this website.

Nice, easy dish to make. I did half the amount of balsamic (as another reviewer suggested), after trying it first with less and it was perfect. (I love balsamic but it can over-power a dish with too much imho). The second time I made this I added sliced onions with the garlic and it worked well. Thanks for the recipe!

I didn't have a whole pound of cremini mushrooms, so I approximated the amount of other ingredients proportionally. I found that cooking for a total of 6 minutes wasn't nearly enough -- I needed closer to 10 minutes. In any case the result was delicious. Next time I'll try adding some diced shallot and dry basil or oregano.

OK, I turned this in to a yum for an appetizer. It would be good by itself on top of balsamic chicken or steak, but too blah as a stand alone for me. So, added some minced shallots, a little white pepper, a little cayene pepper, 1 chopped portobello and some more balsamic and reduced the mixture down a bit. I removed stems from cleaned mushroom caps and cooked the mushrooms in the mixture making sure not to break them for about 5 minutes. I took the mushrooms out, put them on a baking sheet. I poured the mixture in 1 cup of creme cheese at room temp and some feta. I stuffed the mushrooms and cooked for 20 minutes at 400. They were fab, especially for non-meat eating party goers. The portobello tastes like bits of meat. It was fab.

I made it just like the recipe with the exception of diced onions which I sautéed first. I had some Pinot Grigio and with the balsamic vinegar I thought these tasted great I didn’t add salt or pepper they were perfect just as they were

Love this recipe I made it as written first but have made some slight changes. My changes is I use a tablespoon of olive oil and on tablespoon butter, I carmelize shallots first then add garlic the garlic and mushrooms.

This is a great accompaniment for grilled steaks. I've made a mushroom side for steak with dry sherry for a long, long time. This combination of garlic and balsamic will replace it for grilled beef. BTW, I cooked it longer than the recipe states reducing the liquid.

These "Balsamic Mushrooms" have an extraordinarily beautiful presentation: caramel color with deep brown ridges. If I were to make this recipe again I would want to add a lot of caramelized onions to give it a more complex flavor and to sop up the juices. My mushrooms were very wet (served in a small bowl with sauce) despite removing the mushrooms from the heat to boil off the excess water before adding the balsamic vinegar and wine. I can easily imagine that these mushrooms would taste better the next day. Thank you CHRISTYJ for sharing your recipe.

Loved it. I used red wine because it was all I had. I added the garlic later, after the mushrooms had cooked a bit because I like a stronger garlic taste. Also used baby portabella mushrooms. Will make again soon!

I had 1.5 lbs of baby portobellos. I sliced them thick, and upped the amount of balsamic and white wine (you can never have too much of that!). This is a pot you have to watch - mushrooms can overcook very quickly. The portobellos stood up nicely to the recipe and kept some firmness which is mt preference.
Sweet and hearty mushrooms.I cut them thick but with this flavor it goes great with steak
Made as written and these were perfect. Simple and delicious!
These were amazing!!!

These were very tasty. Easy to make, but the balsamic vinegar made these sweet rather than savory. I would not plan to make to have with meat. However, I would cut the mushrooms in half and use as an appetizer.
came good, i use red wine, as it was what i had, and i added some chopped cilentro.

Great recipe!! 
Was delicious!
This is now my to go to recipe for mushrooms, simply delicious!

I dint have white wine so I used cooking sherry as a suppose sub everything else remained the same . Wife didnt like the dish by itself but when eaten witha steak she said it was really good I may tone down the baslamic vinegar next time .
